criteria.description: Correctly differentiates and substitutes to get xdd = A^2x + ABu + Budot.
Correctly explains the direct-vs-indirect distinction between B and AB.

solutions.fullSolution:
xdd = A*xdot + B*udot = A(Ax+Bu) + B*udot = A^2x + ABu + B*udot.
x_i is influenced by u directly through row i of B (no A factor). xdd_i is influenced by u only after passing through the dynamics matrix A once (via row i of AB): u first moves some xdot_j through B, and A then propagates that into xdd_i, hence 'indirect.' Stacking B, AB, A^2B, ... as columns of C collects every level of directness.
AB = [[0,0],[1,0]]@[1,0]^T = [0,1]^T. C = [B AB] = [[1,0],[0,1]], the 2x2 identity, rank 2. (Independently verified with NumPy while authoring this module.)

Discriminant Kd^2-4mKp = 1-16 = -15 < 0, complex roots. Re(omega) = -Kd/(2m) = -1/2 = -0.5, negative, so asymptotically stable (oscillatory-damped). (Independently verified with NumPy eigenvalue computation while authoring this module: eigenvalues -0.5 +/- 1.936j.)

criteria.description: Correctly applies the product rule to compute Vdot.
Correctly substitutes the closed-loop dynamics and simplifies to -Kd*qdot^2, noting the cancellation.

solutions.fullSolution:
Vdot = m*qdot*qddot + Kp(q-q*)qdot.
Substitute m*qddot = -Kp(q-q*)-Kd*qdot: m*qdot*qddot = -Kp(q-q*)qdot - Kd*qdot^2.
Vdot = [-Kp(q-q*)qdot - Kd*qdot^2] + Kp(q-q*)qdot = -Kd*qdot^2. The Kp(q-q*)qdot terms cancel exactly. (Independently verified symbolically with SymPy while authoring this module.)
